annotations.title: Start a post with an interview

description: Requires a TechFabric engineer's Microsoft sign-in (scope blog.write). Start here when asked to write, draft or start a blog post or case study for techfabric.com, before writing anything, even inside the techfabric-web repository (never a local file): brainstorm mode (one question about real work first: what happened, what surprised you), then the interview for a post, a case study or an explainer, about seven questions tailored to the topic and to today's brief. First look through the repository, and the site with search and get_page, then send suggested (your answers from what you found) so the engineer only confirms or corrects; it also offers what techfabric.com already published on the topic (published). With form: true, a client that answers forms and shows no apps shows them as one form; otherwise ask them in chat and call again with answers. Returns their answers as sources for submit_draft, then outline and check_outline before any prose. A read: nothing is filed or claimed.

answers.description: The engineer's own answers, by question id, word for word, once they've given them in chat: returned as sources for submit_draft.

brief.description: Tailor the questions to the brief the engineer holds today (get_brief claims one; this only reads it).

form.description: true: in a client that shows forms and no MCP Apps view, ask the engineer the interview as one form. Send it only when the engineer wants a form; left out, the questions come back to ask in chat.

kind.description: What the engineer is writing: "post" (the default), "case-study", or "explainer" (a post on news or a feature; submit it as kind "post").

post_type.description: The post type, which sets the opening rule and how hard the fact-check reads it. story (the default): work someone at TechFabric did. The opening has TechFabric doing that work by paragraph two, and every claim gets the full fact-check. perspective: a talk or conference the author attended, a conversation with an industry leader, others' work, or our view of what's possible. TechFabric's view by paragraph two ("we think", "we'd", "I believe" count). What a speaker or another company said is attributed in the sentence ("In her demo, ...") and must match what the author provided; forward-looking views need no source. whats-new: a new feature in AI, Databricks or related tech, and how it could help future projects. Open on what changed (its date and source), then our view. Product facts (name, preview or GA, date, what it does) are checked against the vendor's docs or release notes; forward-looking views need no source. personal: the author's own essay or position, in the first person, about where the work or the industry is going and what people should do. Opening and fact-check as perspective, and the only type that may say "I believe", address the reader as "you", bold up to three thesis sentences, make one "this is not X" thesis reframe and close on a call to act. Never for an engineer explaining a feature or their own project. Choose personal only when the engineer writes in their own voice about a position, never for an engineer explaining a feature or their project. Left out, it is story; an explainer is always whats-new. Not for a case study.

suggested.description: Your suggested answer to each question, by its id, from the repository and the engineer's notes: shown to them to confirm or correct, never sent as their words.

topic.description: What it is about, in the engineer's words. Leave it out with brief: true.

name: start_post

ask_how.description: form: the engineer answered the form; chat: ask them these questions in chat; answered: the answers came with the call

brainstorm.description: How to brainstorm with the engineer before any outline: one focused question at a time, about real work

answer_id.description: The answers key for the engineer's answer to first_question, kept in the sources like the rest

missing.description: Required questions still unanswered: ask the engineer for these before the outline

mode.description: The writing partner's mode (editorial/voices-of-techfabric.md): brainstorm first, draft only when asked

post_type.description: The post type this interview is for: what the call sent, else story (whats-new for an explainer). Not for a case study

post_type_question.description: When the call sent no post_type: ask the engineer this, with your suggestion, and send their choice as post_type to check_outline, lint_draft and submit_draft

published.description: What techfabric.com already published on the topic (posts, case studies, service pages), from the site's own index: offered to the engineer to confirm, never as their words

sources.description: The engineer's answers, word for word, as the text to send as sources with submit_draft and update_draft

voice.description: How every sentence is said (editorial/voices-of-techfabric.md, "Before you write a sentence"): follow it in the outline, the draft and every rewrite.

title: Start a post with an interview
